The series is trend-dominated with unstable rankings; a robust trimmed mean may help by discarding outlier model forecasts.
The series is trend-dominated with unstable rankings; a simple mean may offer a baseline different from trimmed/weighted.
Test a robust weighted combo with softmax_neg_error to see if it improves over trimmed_mean, given the unstable rankings and trend-dominated regime.
The series has unstable rankings and a strong trend; a robust median may outperform trimmed mean.
Use a different combination type (DBA) to explore a robust averaging method for this trend‑dominated, highly predictable series with unstable rankings.
The series has unstable rankings and a strong trend; a per-horizon best-per-horizon weighting may capture changing dominance across horizons.
The series is trend-dominated with unstable rankings, so a per‑horizon weighted combo that picks the best few models per step may capture changing strengths without overfitting.
Ranking is unstable and multiple correlated groups exist, so a forward‑selection weight (w5) may pick complementary models better than a global weighted mean.
Try a robust weighted combo using a very low-concentration inverse-error handle (w7) to reduce variance in this unstable ranking trend-dominated series.
The series shows unstable ranking and strong trend; a dynamic weight that adapts to error trends might capture improvements over time, so try weighted with error_trend.
The series is trend-dominated with unstable rankings; a per-horizon mean of the top 3 models per step may capture complementary strengths without overfitting to a single model.

decision.justification: Selected 'trimmed_mean' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.8842. Series context: trend strength 0.8766 and seasonal strength 0.1395; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau 0.025); 1 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 3.3.
